pins.definition: To have your home in a place.
To have one's home in a particular place or live in a particular way.
To have your home in a particular place.

situation: A family of four sits together in the cosy living room of their own house: a father reading in an armchair, a mother knitting on the sofa, and two children playing a board game on the carpet; a lamp is lit and the window shows the house's front garden. The room feels lived in, with family photos on the wall and slippers by the door.
subject: a family living at home

prompt: A family of four sits together in the cosy living room of their own house: a father reading in an armchair, a mother knitting on the sofa, and two children playing a board game on the carpet; a lamp is lit and the window shows the house's front garden. The room feels lived in, with family photos on the wall and slippers by the door. loose watercolour washes over confident ink linework, blooms and granulation in the pigment, warm paper grain, the warmth of a picture book for adults. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
